newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Europe likely to monitor HK human rights - lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: Europe likely to monitor HK human rights - lawmaker.

text.p: The European Union might launch an annual human rights report on Hong Kong after China takes back the British colony, a Hong Kong legislator said on Monday.

Andrew Cheng of the territory's popular Democratic Party said EU's commissioner for external relations Hans van den Broek gave assurances that the union would consider the move, to be implemented after the handover at midnight on June 30.

"They are considering and would like to do it after (June 30) 1997, to monitor human rights issues when the British government is gone," Cheng said after returning from a trip to the seat of the European parliament at Strasbourg, France, with a group of human rights activists.
"He (van den Broek) said this can be considered but it hasn't been confirmed yet," Cheng said
Many residents of this territory of 6.4 million people are worried they will lose their freedoms and democratic rights.

On Sunday, China's parliament published a list of 25 Hong Kong laws, including those allowing democratic elections and protecting civil liberties, which would be scrapped or amended after the sovereignty transfer.

Cheng, who made the trip together with two representatives from the group Hong Kong Human Rights Monitor, said that the report would be in the interest of European politicians and businessmen working in Hong Kong.

"Human rights is an international practice and issue...for any country whose statesmen and businessmen are in Hong Kong, I think it is in their interest to know what is happening in Hong Kong after 1997," Cheng said.
